author: TEDx Talks
description:
Human brains define who people are. They serve as containers for knowledge, skills, and cherished memories. They enable communication, relationships, movement, and understanding of the world. Over the course of a lifetime, one in four individuals will experience a stroke, which often results in brain damage. The consequences of this damage can have an enormous impact on quality of life, and stroke remains one of the leading causes of adult disability worldwide.

Historically, scientists and clinicians believed the brain had a very limited capacity to recover. However, recent decades of research have revealed a remarkable degree of plasticity that can facilitate re-learning and rehabilitation following damage. Healthy regions of the brain can be encouraged to take on the functions of damaged areas.

This talk introduces research on new ways to interact with the damaged human brain using brain-computer interfaces to harness this intrinsic plasticity and promote better recovery. Dr Kathy
title: A new approach to stroke recovery research | Kathy Ruddy | TEDxQueensUniversityBelfast

author: TEDx Talks
description: After a transport company remotely disabled the microchip implanted in his hand, geneticist and biohacker Meow-Ludo found himself at the centre of a legal and ethical battle over bodily autonomy, technology, and human rights. In this provocative talk, he explores the frontlines of a future where corporations may hold unprecedented power over the technology woven into our bodies. As the line between human and machine rapidly disappears, Meow-Ludo asks a question that will affect every one of us sooner than we think: who gets to control the future of being human? Meow-Ludo Meow-Meow is a transdisciplinary bio-artist and geneticist who challenges the boundaries between human bodies, technology, and law. With a BSc in Genetics and MBA, he founded Australia's first DIY biotechnology laboratory and has raised over $2M across multiple biotech ventures, securing five Australian patents in diagnostic technology. His work spans molecular biology, speculative design, and bodily autonomy advocacy
title: Cyborg Rights: The Next Human Rights Movement | Meow-Ludo Meow-Meow | TEDxSutherland

author: TEDx Talks
description: We don't often think of music as "colorful," but AI music algorithms are now showing what happens when that color is left out. If you want to dive into the meaning of music or what it means for music to be colorful, you would be a lovely audience member to have for this presentation. Benjamin Honeray Lee is a musician and computer science PhD student at Tsinghua SIGS. He has previously published research in mathematical music theory and now studies the interdiscipline between these two fields under the mentorship of Prof. Wu Zhiyong. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: AI Music is "colorless." Here's how we can fix it. | Benjamin Honeray Lee | TEDxTsinghua SIGS

author: TEDx Talks
description: Most of us heard the “normal” distribution for the first time in high school or freshman year in university when our performance in a course was measured via a Bell-shaped curve. It is called “normal” since it is believed that all natural phenomena follow this statistical law. This assumption rules every human-made system from telecommunications to water dams, from energy grids to satellite missions. The reign of ‘normality’ in our engineering minds goes hand in hand with our societal sub-conscious association of positive meanings with being ‘normal.’ Normal is unthreatening, predictable, easy. However, the very same societies also demand best performance in professional life, in exams, in profits, etc and the engineering systems aim for the best performance. A whole myth around the average, that is the mean statistics while what is asked for is maximum, that is the extreme statistics. In this brief talk, we will challenge this contradiction and provoke questions on whether AI needs t
title: Is this world normal? A Skeptical Probabilist View | Ercan (尔江) Engin Kuruoglu | TEDxTsinghua SIGS

author: TEDx Talks
description:
A small burn on my hand once changed the way I see our planet. The pain lasted for days, and I came to realize something profound that if a tiny burn can hurt us so deeply, what must the Earth feel when we scorch her forests, poison her waters, and strain her strength for our comfort? In this talk, I share how I came to see the Earth not as an environment, but as a generous mother, patient, and quietly hurting. Through personal experiences and the truths hidden in our daily lives, I invite the audience to feel what the planet feels, to see our impact, and to rediscover the love and spirit needed to protect the only home we all share. My goal is to help people understand sustainability not as a technical agenda or policy framework, but as a story of connection, a story of responsibility, gratitude, and the simple human decision to care for the home that has cared for us since the beginning and asks almost nothing in return.
 I’m Abdul Samad (杜文康) from Pakistan, a researcher in Smart Lo
title: Motherland: The Home We All Share | Abdul Samad | TEDxTsinghua SIGS

author: TEDx Talks
description: In 1835, Darwin’s discoveries in the Galápagos, made during HMS Beagle’s voyage, sowed the seed for evolution theory—born not on land but at sea, which has long been humanity’s great teacher. Today, the ocean offers solutions to global crises: wave/tidal energy for clean power, seabed minerals as sustainable resources, and underwater spaces for overcrowded cities. The talk shows it is the right time for young civil engineers to shift to ocean engineering, using their skills to build wave farms and eco-friendly underwater habitats, answering the ocean’s call to shape a sustainable future. Li Sunwei is an Associate Professor at the Institute for Ocean Engineering, Shenzhen International Graduate School (SIGS) Tsinghua University. Funded by the China Scholarship Council, he pursued and completed his doctoral degree Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering, Western University in Canada. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organize
title: Education in Ocean Engineering is Right On Time | Sunwei Li | TEDxTsinghua SIGS

author: TEDx Talks
description: The global scale of food waste is staggering, with over 1 billion tons generated annually. However, this organic-rich waste stream presents immense potential for resource recovery and valorization. This report highlights recent R&D efforts aimed at converting urban food waste into valuable resources products. Innovative outputs include biodegradable plastics, paper and fibrous materials, and high-quality electrode carbon for energy-storage batteries. By producing marketable products and closing the waste loop, these technological advancements offer promising new perspectives for advancing the circular economy and achieving sustainable food waste utilization. Prof. Xiaoyan Li is a distinguished Professor at Tsinghua Shenzhen International Graduate School and a globally renowned researcher in Environmental Science and Engineering. He is a recipient of China's Long-term Innovation Talent Program and is ranked among Stanford University's World's Top 2% Scientists. Prof. Li's impactful res
title: Turning Food Waste into Value-Added Products | Xiaoyan (李晓岩) Li | TEDxTsinghua SIGS

author: TEDx Talks
description: Our planet is being choked by pollution, starting on land and ending in our oceans. Today, plastics already outnumber fish, and waste glass has become a silent but equally dangerous threat. Both materials break   down into micro-particles that devastate marine life, disrupt ecosystems, and ultimately return to us through the food chain, harming human health. In this talk, I will present practical strategies to curb plastic and glass pollution, emphasizing the power of technology, scientific innovation, and circular material design. I will also share details from my own research, where waste glass is transformed into high-value functional materials and high-performance adsorbents for environmental remediation. This is a journey from waste to resource, from problem to possibility, showing how rethinking materials can help restore our oceans and safeguard our future. Dr. Jean-Baptiste Mawulé Dassekpo, a national of the Republic of Benin, holds a PhD in Civil Engineering from the Harbin I
title: Saving Our Planet from Plastic & Glass Pollution | Jean-Baptiste Mawulé Dassekpo | TEDxTsinghua SIGS

The talk presents model-driven information, strategy and technology aimed at assessing and designing ecosystem fitness by encoding socio-ecological teleconnected value and systemic compounding risk into ecosystem’s ecohydrological structures that are self-emerging and adaptable. An echo-logic call for nature-positive ecohydrological design across habitats and sectors including enhanced restoration and adaptation, urban regeneration, and climate de-novo ecosystem creation for the collective good. An initiative for an eco-intelligence global effort to make the planet we need. title: EcoWeave: The Vital Stitches of Nature’s Design | Matteo Convertino | TEDxTsinghua SIGS

author: TEDx Talks
description: Most residences look similar, but our lives are all different. In this talk, we ask a simple question: what if your home didn't come off a standard template, but actually got to know you? We'll explore how AI can personalise housing end-to-end — from how spaces are designed and built, to how they adapt in real time to your habits, comfort and needs. This isn't about adding a few "smart" devices; it's about turning your whole home into an intelligent partner that understands you. Dr Shuai Lu is an Associate Professor at Shenzhen International Graduate School, Tsinghua University. His research has long focused on the intersection of architecture and computing (AI4DESIGN). This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: When Your Home Knows You: AI and the Future of Personalised Living | Shuai Lu | TEDxTsinghua SIGS

author: TEDx Talks
description: I share my journey of embracing the "AI plus" wave at the age of 36, after transitioning from a decade-long career in architecture to academia. Through my exploration of AI-driven design and large language models (LLMs), I show how technology is reshaping the architectural process. Join me as I discuss how AI can empower architects to unlock new possibilities, collaborate creatively, and revolutionize the future of design. My name is Liu Minjuan, and I am currently pursuing a Master's degree in Architecture at Tsinghua University, where I focus on AI-driven intelligent environments and human-centered design. Before returning to academia, I spent ten years as a professional architect, working in both Shenzhen and Singapore. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: Reborn at 36 with AI | Minjuan Liu | TEDxTsinghua SIGS

description:
In this TEDx talk, Penelope explores perfectionism through the analogy of a toxic relationship: one that begins as motivation but slowly tells people to hold back from their passions whilst silently burning them out . Combining personal stories with psychological research, she shows how letting go of the pressure and keeping the challenge can finally set people free. Penelope sheds light on the silent struggle of perfectionism
and encourages breaking free from it to unlock
creativity and reduce self-imposed pressure. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: Perfectionism: the breakup you never knew you needed | Penelope Deschamps | TEDxJCG Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description: I have a big dream - to dedicate my life to the thing I like most, acting. I haven’t always been supported in my endeavours by other people who are convinced it is too difficult for me to achieve. But why can’t I be part of the 2% of actors who earn a living wage and make their passion their life? The things we are told by others can shape how we view ourselves and what we can achieve. Being surrounded by people who don’t have your interests at heart can make you doubt and second-guess your choices, but following your heart based on your dreams is the way to stay faithful to yourself and not do something that doesn’t fulfil you. I want others to listen to my story and think about their own lives, not letting external influences dictate how they choose what is right for them. Because the failure rate if you never try is, after all, 100%. I am a teenager from Jersey, Channel Islands who loves being creative, stepping out of my comfort zone and being with others who energise and empower
title: Why you shouldn’t give up on your dreams - or yourself  | Penny Le Maistre | TEDxJCG Youth

As young people, we are often boxed into stereotypes; lazy, arrogant, selfish. I want to give a new perspective, reframing teenage life through an economic lens, revealing pressures and costs adults often overlook. Understanding the hidden costs brings empathy, patience and hopefully, less stereotypes around being a teenager. 
 I am an A level student in Jersey and I study Maths, Economics and Spanish. I have a passion for languages and Economics and chose to base my talk on the costs of being a young person today through an economic lens, offering a new perspective. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

author: TEDx Talks
description:
In my talk, I explore how sport is about much more than competition or winning. Through my own experiences in netball, I’ve learned that sport teaches important life skills such as resilience, confidence, teamwork, kindness, and how to deal with failure. I want to show that the value of sport goes far beyond the court, and that by changing how we think about it, more people may feel confident to take part without the fear of not being good enough. 
 My name is Mimi and I am a student studying English Literature, Psychology and Health & Social Care. I am also a passionate netball player. Sport has been a huge part of my life and has taught me far more than just physical skills. Through netball, training, and challenges, I have developed resilience, confidence, teamwork and kindness. These experiences inspired me to speak about how sport can shape who we are as people, not just as athletes. I hope my talk encourages others to see sport differently and recognise the life lessons it can t
title: Sport as a Life Subject  | Mimi Carney | TEDxJCG Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description: Self-improvement sounds like a good thing — so how does it sometimes lead people toward extremism? Anderson Han explores how online self-improvement culture can be hijacked by hidden agendas, and what young people can do to stay grounded in their own goals. Anderson Han is a junior who has been seeing a concerning rise in extremism among young men due to self-improvement content on social media. After a few encounters with it himself, and observing a friend going through the same situation, he feels compelled to share the dangers associated with self-improvement online, and the steps you can take to combat it. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: Self-Improvement & Extremism | Anderson Han | TEDxNHHS Youth

When we reach major crossroads, the path forward isn't always clear. Often, it feels like a mystery wrapped in a metaphor. She shares insights on how to embrace uncertainty, pivot and find clarity in the unpredictable Widely recognized for her leading roles in Indian television series like Naagin and Amrit Manthan, Adaa Khan has built a career defined by versatility. At TEDxIITHyderabad, she shares her journey of navigating the entertainment industry, balancing personal growth with the demands of public identity. description: What happens when one of the most competitive athletes on Earth stops chasing the wave just for himself? In this deeply personal talk, two-time world champion surfer Tom Carroll reflects on the relentless pursuit of being on the “inside” of the wave — and the unexpected freedom, clarity, and connection he discovered when he learned to share it instead. Blending his stories from an impressive surfing career, philosophy, and the human search for meaning, Tom reveals why sharing may be the very thing that allows us to truly thrive.  Tom Carroll is an Australian former professional surfer and two-time world champion, known for his powerful and radical style in the 1980s. He won the ASP World Tour in 1983 and 1984, and also achieved three Pipeline Masters victories in ’87, ’90 & ’91. Beyond his competitive success, in 1985 Tom took a stand against the then Apartheid regime in South Africa using this World Champion status to open eyes to humanitarian dislocation. description:
Luck is totally random, right? Well, mostly. But in this hilarious and surprisingly practical talk, Pulkit Kochar argues that while you can't control the universe, you can make yourself a much bigger target for good things to hit. Breaking down a series of his own highly questionable life choices, Kochar introduces the concept of "increasing your surface area of luck."

You might not be lucky, but you can definitely learn how to stand in the right place when the lightning strikes. Pulkit Kochar is a popular Indian digital creator, entertainer, and social media personality known for his witty observational comedy and pop-culture sketches.

He rose to prominence through his relatable content on Instagram and YouTube, often satirizing everyday Indian situations and Bollywood tropes This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

description:
It takes grit to survive the bottom, and courage to jump toward the top. In this deeply personal talk, Mihir Ahuja explores the messy reality of chasing your goals. Comparing the human experience to an ECG machine, he tells us how the dips represent our greatest lessons, and the spikes represent our boldest choices and how stability is not what life actually is. Mihir Ahuja is a rising Indian actor best known for his role as Jughead Jones in Netflix’s The Archies (2023).

After debuting in Super 30 (2019), he gained acclaim for his work in major streaming series like Made in Heaven, Bard of Blood, and the film Vijay 69. Beyond acting, he is a trained beatboxer and model. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. description: Timothy reflects on the tension between self-doubt and overconfidence, and the human desire for definite answers in an uncertain world. Blending personal experience with insights from science and mathematics, the talk explores how certainty can be comforting but limiting. Timothy reframes uncertainty as an inescapable part of reality worth celebrating; not something to eliminate, but a tool that can shape perspective and meaning. Timothy Ma is a student at Trinity Grammar School. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

author: TEDx Talks
description: Mahd reflects on failing a maths test and realising that a teacher's kindness - giving back marks to pass - had an unintended effect: it removed the pressure instead of teaching him how to push through it. Blending personal experience with research on stress inoculation, the talk argues that we have swapped resilience for "safetyism," mistaking discomfort for danger. It reframes stress not as a sign of weakness, but as something we can face and concludes that resilience is forged in the struggle, not in quitting. Muhammad is a student at Trinity Grammar School. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: Teaching teens to manage stress, not fear it | Muhammad Mahd Ansari | TEDxTrinity Grammar School

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Nesta talk o autor argumenta que a proteção contemporânea deve ser invisível, funcionando de forma silenciosa para salvaguardar a democracia e a liberdade sem recorrer à vigilância intrusiva. 

São destacados perigos críticos como a desinformação, a manipulação algorítmica e a erosão dos direitos civis que ameaçam as sociedades modernas. Para enfrentar estes desafios, propõe-se um esforço coletivo assente no reforço da literacia digital e na exigência de transparência tecnológica por parte dos cidadãos. Enfatiza-se ainda a necessidade de uma liderança ética e exemplar, capaz de promover a confiança e a cooperação em vez do controlo pelo medo. 

Por fim, defende-se que a segurança mais eficaz é aquela que se sente através da liberdade responsável, exigindo uma participação ativa e consciente de toda a comunidade.

 António Gameiro Marques é licenciado em Ciências Militares Navais e especializado em Comunicações, tendo frequentado um mestrado em Engenharia Eletrotécnica e de Computadore
title: A verdadeira segurança não é a que se vê, é a que se sente! | António Gameiro Marques | TEDxPorto

author: TEDx Talks
description:
José Avillez partilha a história do salmonete que mudou a sua vida e como os nossos padrões se constroem nos momentos em que ninguém está a ver. Uma reflexão sobre brio, hábito e a pergunta que devíamos todos fazer a nós próprios.

 José Avillez é chef e tem como missão promover a gastronomia portuguesa e afirmar Portugal como um destino gastronómico de excelência. Considerado uma das grandes referências da cozinha nacional, tem-se destacado pelo espírito empreendedor e pela constante vontade de ir mais além.

Detém vários restaurantes em Lisboa, Cascais, Dubai e Macau, todos com conceitos únicos, mas com um ponto em comum: a sua paixão pela cozinha. O Belcanto, em Lisboa, é o seu restaurante mais emblemático, distinguido com duas estrelas Michelin, três Sóis Repsol e classificado como o 42.º melhor restaurante do mundo pela The World’s 50 Best Restaurants.

A sua visão criativa estende-se a espaços como o Encanto, o Mini Bar, o Bairro do Avillez, o Cantinho do Avillez, o Maré, a Tasc
title: Excelência no invisível | José Avillez | TEDxPorto

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Nunca se falou tanto como hoje de inclusão, tolerância, respeito pelas diferenças, mas será que esses princípios estão a ser aplicados à personalidade/comportamento das pessoas?

O que dizem, por exemplo, as neurociências da felicidade, motivação, liderança, trabalho em equipa, etc? Será que poderemos ser todos felizes, motivados, resilientes? O que diz a ciência sobre isto? Seremos “negativos” ou “infelizes” porque queremos ou porque não podemos? Estaremos a respeitar essas pessoas? A ser tolerantes com essas diferenças?

 José Soares é Professor Catedrático de Fisiologia na Universidade do Porto e uma referência quando falamos de performance humana, seja no desporto de alto rendimento, seja no mundo corporativo. Ao longo da sua carreira, acompanhou pilotos de carros e MotoGP, trabalhou com diversas empresas e é atualmente especialista do projeto FUEL da Deloitte. Adicionalmente, é consultor do Motor and Sport Institute, em Madrid, e do projeto IRON FIT YOU, no Brasil.

title: O que diz a "hard science" sobre "soft skills" | José Soares | TEDxPorto

title: Psicopatas - para além do bem e do mal | Henrique Prata Ribeiro | TEDxPorto

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Assumimos como missão a tarefa delicada de escrever para os mais novos porque valorizamos a leitura e valorizamos as crianças. Sabíamos que só consegue ler bem quem pratica a leitura porque encontra livros que lhe agradam. Procurámos contribuir também como escritoras. 

Mas como escrever para crianças? Depois de muito conversarmos, ficou assente que fosse qual fosse a história: o texto seria leve, límpido, transparente para criar imagens sugestivas na mente dos leitores; as personagens seriam apresentadas com um recorte nítido, para que ganhassem vida e passassem a fazer parte do grupo de amigos próximos; o enredo seria imaginado de modo a interessar e, se possível, a absorver o leitor que, lendo, sentisse que fazia parte da história.

 Ana Maria Magalhaes é uma figura incontornáveis da literatura infantojuvenil portuguesa e da promoção da leitura, reconhecidas pela sua longa carreira como educadoras, investigadoras e autoras.

Ana Maria Magalhães, por sua vez, foi nomeada Técnica do
title: Escrever para formar leitores | Ana Maria Magalhães & Isabel Alçada | TEDxPorto

author: TEDx Talks
description:
O que está realmente em falta no sistema educativo atual? Nesta talk, apresentamos o Programa MentorART, o projeto vencedor do TEDxPorto Award 2026, que propõe uma resposta à falta de quem veja, quem escute e quem acredite. A desigualdade socioeducativa é apresentada não apenas como um atraso académico, mas como um défice de "capital humano" que custa ao país centenas de milhões de euros em talento desperdiçado.

A talk explora a mentoria como uma "tecnologia relacional" essencial. Através de uma estrutura rigorosa, este programa liga estudantes universitários e profissionais a jovens dos 10 aos 16 anos, criando alianças de aprendizagem que reduzem comportamentos de risco em 50% e aumentam as hipóteses de prosseguimento de estudos avançados. A mentoria é cidadania ativa com um retorno social de investimento superior a x10.

Ao partilhar o percurso de transformação de jovens acompanhados pelo Programa, a talk demonstra como o apoio individualizado permite que estes se tornem visíveis p
title: Vencedor do TEDxPorto Award 2026: Programa MentorART | Luana Martucci | TEDxPorto

author: TEDx Talks
description:
A erotização precoce na infância é um fenómeno crescente que expõe crianças a conteúdos inadequados. Este cenário pode ter um impacto negativo na  saúde emocional, autoestima e no relacionamentos. Por isso, é essencial compreender suas causas e fortalecer o papel de toda a comunidade no seu enfrentamento.

 Vânia Beliz é psicóloga clínica e sexóloga, com especialização em educação para a sexualidade. É licenciada em Psicologia Clínica, mestre em Sexologia e doutorada em Estudos da Criança, tendo dedicado a sua carreira à promoção da saúde sexual e reprodutiva ao longo do ciclo de vida.
